A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ELICIT research, with matching authors, framework, and principal experiments. All pages, including appendices, tables, figures, and equations, were readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, unseen-task experiments, BM25 integration results, and intervention and retrieval ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds selective-activation analyses, additional model and task evaluations, method variants, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The main library, retriever, thresholding, and intervention pipeline remains unchanged. Appendices L and M introduce experimental variants using Sentence-BERT-based diverse demonstration selection and distributing intervention strength across three or all layers. These are limited procedural extensions.

E1.justification: Appendix K, Table 14 adds GSM8K as an in-domain task and MMLU-Professional-Law as an out-of-domain task. The original 20-task benchmark, five unseen tasks, and existing evaluation scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain zero-shot, 16-shot ICL, and BM25, while the existing similarity-based retrieval comparisons also remain. The new diversity and intervention variants are component ablations rather than additions to the independent baseline set.

E3.justification: New experiments evaluate Pythia-6.9B, Pythia-12B, Llama3-70B, and Llama3-8B-Instruct, introduce forced activation and multi-layer controls, and measure processing time by pipeline stage. This substantially broadens experimental settings. Newly documented splits and sample counts do not establish changes to the original experiments' protocols.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, Appendix J adds selected-vector counts, an ARC-Challenge case, forced-activation tests, and library-usage frequencies. Appendices L, M, and N add demonstration-diversity sensitivity, multi-layer intervention comparisons, and runtime decomposition. These substantially expand evidence about mechanisms, design choices, and practical costs.

E5.justification: V1 already reports plus/minus quantities but does not specify a seed count. V2's Tables 2 and 3 newly state that evaluation uses three random seeds. This improves reporting without establishing an increase in runs or introducing confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 3, 4, and 9 undergo extensive numerical revisions. For example, Table 4's Llama3 averages change from BM25 44.9 versus BM25+ELICIT 45.6 to 55.8 versus 53.1, reversing the reported ranking. Numerous appendix results are also added. The PDFs do not explain the cause of the broad numerical revisions, so these are reported-result changes rather than established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Definitions 3.1–3.2, Lemma 3.3, Remark 3.4, and their equations are retained. Appendix A.1 adds a qualitative circuit-interaction hypothesis, without new formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about modular task-vector storage and retrieval, efficient adaptation, selective activation, and generalization. The introduction updates a supporting Pythia result, while substantive qualifications to BM25 integration appear in the results interpretation.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 replaces the interpretation of consistent BM25 benefits with model-size-dependent mixed outcomes and a representation-interference explanation. New appendices discuss possible circuit competition, selective activation mechanisms, instruction-tuned models' prompt sensitivity and evaluation difficulties, and trade-offs from diverse demonstrations. These materially expand explanations and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendix I newly documents dataset-specific partitioning rules and minimum training/test sizes; Tables 2–3 disclose 100 examples per task. V2 also clarifies random demonstration selection, documents the new variants, and supplies stage-level timings. The abstract changes code availability from a future promise to reported public availability. These substantially improve reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: V2 adds visual and multimodal task-vector research to Section 2 and references supporting the new circuit, instruction-tuning, and demonstration-selection discussions. The central positioning of ELICIT as an external modular task-vector library remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include localized rewriting of Section 4.5, shorter explanatory additions, new appendix subsections, acknowledgements, and affiliation/header edits. The main section sequence, most existing prose, and extensive prompt documentation remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 10–18 and Figure 16 substantially expand the appendix displays with activation statistics, a worked case, model/task comparisons, intervention variants, and runtime breakdowns. Existing graphics are largely retained; Figure 5 is relocated, Figure 6 gains descriptive panel labels, and several table captions are revised.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, explicit split/sample/seed reporting and direct activation controls and runtime measurements make v2 easier to assess and reproduce. The more qualified BM25 discussion also helps. These gains are limited by unexplained revisions to central results and remaining table–text contradictions: Section 4.5 describes reasoning gains although Table 4 shows Llama3 declining from 68.8 to 62.7, and Table 9's caption claims a Deepmind gain despite 30.7 falling to 26.4. Overall, the added evidence and documentation support a limited net improvement.
